name: Tinea (Fungal Infection / Ringworm)
description: Tinea is a common and contagious fungal skin infection. Despite its name 'ringworm', it is caused by microscopic fungi (dermatophytes), not a worm. It typically appears as an itchy, red or darker ring-shaped rash with clearer skin in the center.
common_symptoms: An itchy, circular or ring-shaped rash with raised, scaly edges
The center of the ring may look clear, flat, or less red than the border
Cracking, scaling, peeling, and maceration between toes (athlete's foot)
Red, intensely itchy rash in groin folds (jock itch)
Rings can expand outward over days and overlap
causes: Fungal dermatophytes (such as Trichophyton, Microsporum, or Epidermophyton) feeding on dead skin keratin
Direct skin-to-skin contact with an infected person, pet (cats/dogs), livestock, or contaminated objects (towels, bedding, gym mats)
risk_factors: Living in warm, humid, tropical or subtropical climates
Excessive sweating and wearing tight, synthetic, damp clothing
Sharing towels, hairbrushes, clothing, or athletic equipment
Walking barefoot in public showers, locker rooms, or swimming pools
first_aid: Wash the infected area with mild soap and water, then pat completely dry with a dedicated towel
Wash hands thoroughly after touching or cleaning the rash
Change out of sweaty clothes immediately into clean, dry cotton garments
precautions: Keep skin clean and dry, especially between toes and in skin folds
Do not share personal items like towels, clothes, hairbrushes, or razors
Wear flip-flops or water shoes in communal showers and locker rooms
Wash clothes, bedding, and towels in hot water
home_care: Keep the affected area thoroughly dry, particularly after bathing
Wear loose-fitting, breathable cotton clothing and underwear
Disinfect sports gear and shared surfaces
do_not: DO NOT apply steroid creams (like hydrocortisone, clobetasol, or combination steroid creams) to fungal rashes; steroids make fungal infections grow worse, spread deeper, and harder to treat (tinea incognito)
DO NOT share towels, socks, bedding, or clothing with family members
DO NOT scratch the rash and then touch other parts of your body
DO NOT walk barefoot in shared locker rooms or communal bathrooms
red_flags: The rash becomes intensely painful, swollen, warm, and leaks yellow pus (secondary bacterial infection)
Spreading red streaks moving up an arm or leg with fever
Fungal infection affecting the scalp with hair loss, swelling, and boggy masses (kerion)
when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor or dermatologist if over-the-counter antifungal cream does not improve the rash within 2 weeks, if the rash spreads widely, or if the scalp or nails are affected.
prevention: Keep skin dry and cool throughout the day
Never share towels, bed sheets, or unwashed clothes
Treat household pets if they show scaly patches or missing fur
Wear clean cotton socks and change them at least once daily
